PG17 BEGIN: "By default (without BEGIN), PostgreSQL executes transactions in 'autocommit' mode, that is, each statement is executed in its own transaction and a commit is implicitly performed at the end of the statement (if execution was successful, otherwise a rollback is done)."
PG17 BEGIN: "BEGIN initiates a transaction block, that is, all statements after a BEGIN command will be executed in a single transaction until an explicit COMMIT or ROLLBACK is given."

PG17 COMMIT: "All changes made by the transaction become visible to others and are guaranteed to be durable if a crash occurs." Executed: ROLLBACK after both INSERTs -> orders_after_rollback 12 (order row gone).

PG17 13.2.1: SELECT "never sees either uncommitted data or changes committed by concurrent transactions during the query's execution" and "SELECT does see the effects of previous updates executed within its own transaction, even though they are not yet committed." Read Committed is the default. Executed: count inside block = 13.

PG17 COMMIT: changes "are guaranteed to be durable if a crash occurs." Holds under the default synchronous_commit = on (round 1 confirmed on the lab container); the lesson does not touch that setting.

PG17 protocol-flow: a failed block needs "Another ROLLBACK ... to restore the session to a usable state." Executed: after the CHECK failure, SELECT 1 -> "ERROR: current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block"; COMMIT answered "ROLLBACK"; count = 12. Claim text is accurate incl. savepoint caveat (END and ABORT also accepted, see issue on section 4 wording).

PG17 53.2.9 Termination: "For either normal or abnormal termination, any open transaction is rolled back, not committed." Executed: quantity-0 run exited 3 after the refusal with the block open; a fresh connection then counted 12.

PG17 13.3.2: "other transactions that attempt UPDATE, DELETE, SELECT FOR UPDATE ... of these rows will be blocked until the current transaction ends"; "Row-level locks are released at transaction end or during savepoint rollback".
Executed stage-0 file unchanged: orders_before 12, orders_inside_transaction 13, orders_after_rollback 12; exit 0.

issues.quote: The four letters ACID name the guarantees; the one that matters most day to day is atomicity.
issues.text: Outline item 4 (track.yaml) is no longer established anywhere in the lesson: the ACID and atomicity bullets were cut in apply-review r4 and nothing replaced them, yet meta coverage.outline_items_covered still lists 4 and outline_items_missing is empty. The scope contract and the lesson disagree.
issues.fix: Owner decision (outline is the contract): either propose deleting outline item 4 from content/tracks/foundation/track.yaml (ACID terms are not in vocab; junior r1 found them unexplained), or propose adding atomicity to vocab and restoring one bullet defining it. Until decided, move 4 to outline_items_missing in meta.

issues.quote: Only `COMMIT` or `ROLLBACK` are still accepted; either one ends the block
issues.text: Too absolute. Executed in a failed block on PG 17.6: END and ABORT were accepted and answered ROLLBACK; ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT is accepted too (claim 8 says so). The ledger claim is right; the lesson sentence overstates it.
issues.fix: Rewrite: 'A statement that ends the block, such as `COMMIT` or `ROLLBACK`, is still accepted; either one ends the block, and a `COMMIT` sent now discards the changes just as `ROLLBACK` would.'

issues.quote: the database returns to the state it had before the `BEGIN`, however many rows the block had already written
issues.text: Overstates claim 5 ('discards every change the transaction made'): changes other connections committed while the block was open stay, so the database as a whole need not be back at its pre-BEGIN state. Same wording in q1 stem ('so the database stands as it did before the BEGIN'); key a stays correct.
issues.fix: Rewrite the bullet end as: 'every change the block made is undone, however many rows it had already written.' In q1 stem (en and vi) replace 'so the database stands as it did before the `BEGIN`' with 'so none of the block's changes remain'.

issues.quote: ACID — the four letters naming the guarantees a transaction carries: atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability.

issues.quote: atomicity — the guarantee that a transaction is indivisible from the outside
issues.text: atomicity is defined but not bolded and is not in vocab; it is then used as 'atomic' in Beginners often think. I can follow it, but it reads as a second new term next to transaction.
issues.fix: Either get atomicity into the lesson's vocab and bold it, or drop the bullet and replace 'each statement is atomic on its own' with 'each statement is all-or-nothing on its own'.

issues.quote: When a statement inside the block fails, PostgreSQL refuses every later command until the block is ended, and the block can no longer be kept: however you end it, none of its changes survive.

issues.fix: Add one sentence: 'Only COMMIT or ROLLBACK are still accepted; either one ends the block, and a COMMIT sent now discards the changes just as ROLLBACK would.'
